## Problem

## Requirements

- Input: one string.
- Output the size of its longest contiguous block made up of the same character.
- Although the request is brief, it may implicitly ask how you would use a character-frequency map.

## Notes

- Boundary conditions: an empty input produces 0, while a one-character input produces 1.

## Preparation

- Review LC 340, "Longest Substring with At Most K Distinct Characters," as the expected follow-up: its prompt looks similar, but its solution strategy is substantially different.

## Hints

<details>
<summary>Hint 1</summary>

Think about scanning the string once and counting consecutive identical characters.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 2</summary>

Use a simple loop with a counter that resets when the character changes.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 3</summary>

The complexity is O(n) time and O(1) space, handle empty input by returning 0.

</details>
